sections.title: A deployed four-city entanglement-based QKD network with real-time key delivery, benchmarked against finite-key security bounds
sections.abstract: The authors report a deployed entanglement-based quantum-key-distribution network across four Slovak cities, with real-time post-processed keys and finite-key performance measurements.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report 13.5 bit/s over 109 km and 4.3 bit/s across 32.1 dB loss on a no-direct-fiber link, with keys delivered after full post-processing.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; deployed telecom fiber, entangled-photon source, simultaneous network links, and the ETSI GS QKD 014 delivery interface
sections.unique_caveat: The authors find the implemented heuristic privacy-amplification scheme can exceed the finite-key bound; their analysis indicates error correction could improve rates, but the longest link has no positive finite-key rate under the implemented scheme.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper cross-lists quantum physics and optics and reports an operating multi-city fiber network; a CiVL news report independently covered the deployment and key-delivery result.

sections.title: JWST Rocky Worlds DDT Observations of LTT 1445 A b and c in Secondary Eclipse Using MIRI/F1500W
sections.abstract: Three JWST/MIRI observing visits and a joint analysis indicate that nearby rocky planet LTT 1445 A b has no substantial atmosphere, while its sibling c remains weakly constrained.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer a CO2 partial pressure below 0.6 mbar and surface pressure at or below about 0.1 bar for planet b; for c, they rule out only thick CO2-bearing atmospheres.
sections.evidence_type: observational; JWST MIRI/F1500W secondary eclipses of both planets across three visits, previous JWST data, and a joint fit including 220 radial velocities
sections.unique_caveat: Planet c’s potentially grazing eclipse and overlapping events leave its depth poorly constrained. The atmospheric limits depend on retrieval and forward-model assumptions and do not exclude every thin or non-CO2 atmosphere.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three independent reductions and a joint fit provide a strong internal cross-check; the result also received independent science-media coverage.

sections.title: Observation of Genuine Multi-Time Quantum Memory
sections.abstract: The authors derive a three-time witness for quantum memory that pairwise tests can miss and demonstrate the hierarchy in a time-continuous superconducting-qubit experiment.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show that a qubit process can admit classical-memory explanations for every pair of times yet fail a jointly evaluated three-time witness, and report an experimental realization on a superconducting-qubit platform.
sections.evidence_type: experimental and theoretical; an analytical three-time witness, channel reconstruction, and a time-continuous superconducting-qubit implementation with time-independent couplings
sections.unique_caveat: The demonstration is a minimal qubit example; the pairwise classical decompositions are supported by numerical optimization and apply to the tested time window and drive regime.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It pairs a new analytical witness with a hardware demonstration; a third-party paper review and research-focused social-media discussion appeared shortly after posting, but these are early discussion signals rather than citation traction.

sections.title: Long-lived light-driven bimagnons at finite momentum in NiO
sections.abstract: Mid-infrared pumping of NiO produces a finite-momentum two-magnon signal whose fitted decay is much slower than previously reported two-magnon coherence times.
sections.claimed_result: The authors measure a pump-induced bimagnon signal peaking about 4 ps after excitation and fit its decay time as 28 ± 11 ps.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; mid-infrared pumping and time-resolved resonant inelastic X-ray scattering at finite momentum
sections.unique_caveat: The delayed growth is interpreted as momentum redistribution rather than directly mapped; the decay time comes from a single-exponential fit over the reported delay range.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper is cross-listed in four physics categories and reports a quantitative time-resolved RIXS result connecting magnetic materials, optical pumping, and quantum dynamics.

sections.title: Observation of the Lambda(1520) suppression in Pb-Pb collisions at sqrt(sNN) = 5.02 TeV
sections.abstract: ALICE measures a central-to-peripheral reduction of the Lambda(1520)/Lambda yield ratio in 5.02 TeV Pb-Pb collisions and compares it with hadronization and transport models.
sections.claimed_result: The measured central-to-peripheral suppression is 0.589 ± 0.015 (stat) ± 0.086 (syst); the authors find the centrality trend is reproduced by MUSIC hydrodynamics coupled to the SMASH hadronic transport afterburner.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; ALICE Pb-Pb collision data at sqrt(sNN) = 5.02 TeV, compared with statistical-hadronization and hydrodynamic-plus-transport calculations
sections.unique_caveat: The systematic uncertainty is material, and the model comparison supports late-stage hadronic effects without uniquely separating rescattering from regeneration.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The collaboration reports a 6.8-sigma significance across six centrality classes, describes this as the first observation of resonance suppression within one collision system, and says the paper was submitted to Physical Review Letters.

sections.title: New measurement of BR(K+ to pi+ nu nubar) at the NA62 experiment
authors: Silvia Martellotti on behalf of NA62 Collaboration
sections.abstract: NA62 presents a new branching-ratio measurement using its 2023–2024 data, which doubles the effective sample and improves sensitivity to the rare K+ to pi+ nu nubar decay.
sections.claimed_result: The full paper reports a combined 2016–2024 branching ratio of 9.6(+1.9/-1.8) × 10^-11, compatible with Standard-Model predictions.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; NA62 kaon-decay data collected at CERN during 2016–2024, including the new 2023–2024 sample
sections.unique_caveat: The combined result has about 20% relative uncertainty; the authors say 2026 data taking and analysis of the full dataset are ongoing.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A new 2023–2024 dataset doubles the effective sample for a rare, precisely predicted decay; the paper’s abstract states an expected sensitivity above 5-sigma for the Standard-Model process, not a 5-sigma observed discovery.

sections.title: Euclid data release 1 (DR1) - SIR spectroscopic calibration
sections.abstract: The Euclid Collaboration describes the SIR calibration pipelines used to reduce NISP slitless spectra for Data Release 1, reporting that current products meet mission requirements.
sections.claimed_result: The authors describe the full-focal-plane calibration pipeline and report that DR1 spectra meet mission requirements, while identifying areas for further optimization.
sections.evidence_type: observational and instrumentation; Euclid/NISP slitless spectroscopy and SIR calibration products for DR1
sections.unique_caveat: The paper documents calibration performance and mission requirements rather than providing a new independent dark-energy constraint; pipeline refinements remain in progress.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: This is a DR1 calibration paper for a major cosmology mission; the authors report more than 170 million validated spectra in red- and blue-grism modes, and the manuscript is submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics.
